planting.note: Set dormant bare-root or container bushes in fall or very early spring in fertile, well-drained soil with some afternoon shade in warmer zones, and prune to an open center each dormant season for airflow.

directions: Jahn's Prairie is a cold-hardy gooseberry selection from Cornell University's Ribes breeding program, drawing on American prairie-type parentage to push hardiness and disease tolerance beyond many European dessert gooseberries. It carries good field resistance to powdery mildew and leaf spot, the two diseases that most limit gooseberry culture in humid eastern gardens, making it a lower-spray option for home growers. Fruit ripens to an amber-pink blush with a sweet-tart flavor suited to fresh eating as well as preserves, borne on a moderately vigorous, upright-to-spreading bush. Site it in full sun to light shade with consistent moisture and a thick mulch layer, since gooseberries dislike hot, dry root zones.
sources: Cornell University Ribes breeding program (Cornell AgriTech, Geneva, NY)
